# requires: transfer
#
# What a failure MEANS, recovered from the record by a reader that did not see
# the error object.
#
# failure-endings.txt beside this file asks what the store did about a failure:
# which state it left the job in, whether it stayed adoptable. This asks the
# other half, and it is the half no transcript could see -- `err=set` is one
# bit, and it says a failure was recorded, never which of the two endings it
# was. A reader rebuilding the error from `error` alone gets a bare string, so
# the refusals this layer declares forever come back retryable and the job is
# fetched again on every sweep for as long as the store exists.
#
# The class and not the sentence, deliberately. Three implementations word an
# error three ways and always will; the class is what a successor branches on
# and it is the same in all three or the layer is not one layer.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=nofetcher
run A alpha
failure A
submit B size=64 digest=good src=missing
run B beta
failure B
submit C size=64 digest=good src=file
run C gamma
failure C

# expect 2: transfer-failed state=failed ... [DL-E2]
# expect 2: content=abstraction.job/base@1,abstraction.job/terminal@1,abstraction.download/failure@1 ... [DL-E16]
# expect 3: ok class=permanent [DL-E16]
# expect 5: transfer-failed state=pending ... [DL-E1]
# expect 5: content=abstraction.job/base@1,abstraction.download/failure@1 ... [DL-E16]
# expect 6: ok class=retryable [DL-E16]
# expect 8: content=abstraction.job/base@1 ... [DL-E16]
# expect 9: ok class=none [DL-E16]
